title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - Pioneer Health
summary: Kickoff POC scoping focused on private networking, data residency and benchmark success criteria. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region selection, egress constraints, expected workload (QPS/tokens), SLOs for latency, and compliance needs (SOC2, KMS). Agreed on benchmarks, timeline (3 week execution + 1 week analysis), and next steps: share networking guide, security docs, and schedule an on-site/remote network walkthrough and initial benchmark run.
topics: POC success criteria: latency & throughput targets, quality baselines
Workload sizing: rps/QPS, average tokens per request, peak patterns
Benchmark plan: synthetic vs replay, datasets, measurement metrics
Private networking options: VPC peering, PrivateLink, Transit Gateway
Regions & data residency: where data must remain, approved cloud regions
Egress constraints: egress-only endpoints, no public internet routes
Security & compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
action_items: Ethan Park: Send Private deployment networking guide + diagram (due: 2027-11-06)
Maya Singh: Prepare initial benchmark plan template and example metrics sheet (due: 2027-11-08)
Omar Khalid: Share VPC CIDR ranges and approved AWS regions for the POC (due: 2027-11-05)
Tasha Reid: Provide list of compliance requirements & KMS architecture constraints (due: 2027-11-06)
Samir Patel: Confirm internal stakeholders and sign-off cadence; confirm pilot success criteria (due: 2027-11-04)
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack and Private networking ops doc
Customer to provide network diagram and permitted regions
Schedule 30-min network walkthrough (calendar invite by Ethan)
Run first benchmark with synthetic traffic next week (SE-led)
Sign NDA / POC agreement before private link setup if needed
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-03 15:00 PT | Duration: 52 mins | Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena, Omar, Tasha, Samir (Pioneer)

Summary: quick kickoff for Pioneer Health POC scoping  focus on private networking & data residency. Lots of Qs on VPC peering vs PrivateLink, egress restrictions, and what benchmarks to run.

[00:00] Ethan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Dr. Lena: Hi I'm Lena, head of AI at Pioneer, we run clinical NLP and patient triage models, excited to scope this POC.
[00:18] Omar: Omar, infra lead, I'll own network setup.
[00:23] Tasha: Tasha, security architect, I'll own compliance asks.
[00:28] Samir: Samir, product, mostly here to align on success criteria and timeline.
[00:33] Ethan: Great, from Redwood Maya and Carlos are with me  Maya will own the benchmarks.
[00:40] Maya: hi all, thanks. quick note, we'll want to understand both steady-state and peak loads.

[01:02] Ethan: high level goal  run a private-networked POC where Pioneer can hit realistic traffic to our Dedicated/Private offering, get latency/cost numbers, and validate data never leaves approved regions. success criteria?
[01:15] Samir: for us it's three things: 95th p50 latency under 350ms for our common prompts, throughput to support 60 QPS peak, and no patient data leaving region. also quality parity with our current in-house model.
[01:35] Maya: ok that's helpful. can you sketch typical request sizes? tokens in/out?
[01:42] Dr. Lena: avg prompt ~250 tokens, responses ~120 tokens, but some longer consultations go up to 1k tokens. avg is more like 370 tokens total.
[01:56] Omar: our traffic pattern is daytime spikes, typical sustained 20-30 QPS, peaks up to 60 for brief periods.

[02:20] Carlos: on networking, two main options: classic VPC peering or PrivateLink (interface endpoints). peering is straightforward but has transitive limitations; PrivateLink gives you a stable endpoint and avoids public egress but needs endpoint setup in each region.
[02:40] Omar: we need it in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 only right now. data residency: all PHI must remain in region and not traverse public internet.
[02:52] Tasha: additionally, we have egress constraints  no DNS resolution to public internet for certain subnets, and all keys must be in our KMS/HSM.

[03:20] Maya: that's fine, Redwood supports VPC Peering for Dedicated and PrivateLink for Private control plane. couple clarifying Qs: do you need cross-account peering or same-account?
[03:30] Omar: cross-account, since our infra is separate.
[03:34] Ethan: note: cross-account VPC peering is supported; for PrivateLink we'll need to provision interface endpoints in your VPC and we can accept the connections from our side.
[03:48] Tasha: latency wise, PrivateLink adds minimal overhead but peering may be faster  is there benchmarking on both?
[03:56] Maya: we have internal numbers, depends on topology. part of the POC can be a head-to-head: peering vs PrivateLink across your regions, measure 50/95/99 pct latencies.

[04:20] Samir: timeline question  how fast could we get a POC running?
[04:24] Carlos: assuming networking info and permissions, bench setup is 3-5 business days; full run + analysis 1-2 weeks. so total 3 weeks ballpark.
[04:36] Dr. Lena: are there any compliance gating items that would delay provisioning?
[04:41] Tasha: we'll need SOC2 evidence, network ACL rules documented, and KMS key policies. also a review of logs retention and auditability.
[04:55] Ethan: we will send our security pack (SOC2 report redacted, data flow diagrams, roles, RBAC, audit log details).

[05:12] Omar: on egress, we cannot allow requests to hit public internet even for telemetry; can Redwood send telemetry over PrivateLink?
[05:20] Maya: yes we can route metrics through the same private endpoints; we also support pushing logs to your S3 via VPC endpoint if you prefer.

[05:40] Samir: benchmarks  what are the standard metrics you'll provide?
[05:44] Maya: we typically provide p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, throughput (QPS), cost per 1k tokens, and error rates. also end-to-end measured from your subnet to our inference engine.

[06:05] Dr. Lena: for quality we'll need a baseline  we have an existing model. can Redwood run a replay of 1k real requests (anonymized) and compare outputs?
[06:15] Maya: yes, we can run replay tests; need a small sample dataset and an eval rubric. we'll measure BLEU-ish metrics where appropriate and human-reviewed quality for clinical flags.

[06:40] Carlos: sizing servers  given 60 QPS peak and 370 avg tokens, we recommend starting with 2 x A100-equivalent workers for Dedicated/private, with burst capacity available. we'll confirm after initial benchmark.

[07:05] Omar: cost concerns  ideally we'd pay for reserved capacity if numbers look good.
[07:10] Ethan: we can propose a Dedicated reserved pool after POC; Redwood Optimize will also recommend quantization/instance types to reduce unit cost.

[07:30] Tasha: encryption  all at-rest and in-transit must be customer-managed KMS. Redwood supports external KMS?
[07:36] Maya: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for hosted there's a managed option but we can arrange bring-your-own-key for Private control plane.

[07:55] Samir: what's the minimal networking we need to provide to start a smoke test?
[08:00] Ethan: CIDR, VPC IDs, a list of subnets for endpoints, and an IAM principal to accept peering/endpoint requests. plus a work account for the SE to run tests.

[08:18] Omar: we'll get CIDRs and subnets this week.

[08:25] Maya: for benchmarks, we'll run three phases: 1) smoke with synthetic traffic to validate connectivity and auth, 2) synthetic load to exercise peak QPS and latency targets, 3) replay with sample anonymized requests for quality comparisons.

[08:48] Dr. Lena: how do you measure tokenization differences across models  we rely on exact token counts for billing.
[08:55] Maya: we report tokens as counted by the deployed model tokenizer; we'll include a tokenization mapping and per-request tokens in the metrics CSV.

[09:10] Carlos: region failover  if you require both us-east-1 and eu-west-1, we'll test cross-region routing; note cross-region egress may cause residency issues so we will keep data in-region for the POC unless you authorize cross-region replication.

[09:33] Tasha: confirm: no logs with PHI leave region; audit logs can be stored in central S3 but masked.
[09:41] Ethan: agreed  we'll mask PHI in any logs and can push raw logs to your S3 in-region if required.

[10:00] Samir: success criteria recap: p95 < 350ms, support 60 QPS peaks, parity to current model on quality metrics, and zero PHI egress.
[10:12] Ethan: yep we'll codify those as acceptance criteria in the POC doc.

[10:30] Omar: any firewall/NACL rules we should prepare?
[10:33] Carlos: we'll provide a checklist  tcp ports, endpoint IP ranges, and TLS SNI requirements. PrivateLink is TLS over ENI so open outbound to endpoint IPs is needed.

[10:50] Tasha: I want to see the KMS key policy and how Redwood accesses keys.
[10:54] Ethan: will include key policy patterns in the security pack.

[11:05] Maya: benchmark schedule suggestion: smoke test Tuesday, synthetic load Wednesday-Thursday, replay Friday; analysis following week.

[11:18] Samir: that timeline works if we get network details by Monday.

[11:25] Omar: we'll aim to provide CIDRs and regions by EOD Monday.

[11:30] Ethan: next steps recap  send security docs, schedule network walkthrough, get CIDRs, schedule benchmark window.

[11:40] Dr. Lena: one last question  in the event of capacity constraints do you have fallback to hosted models in other regions?
[11:48] Carlos: yes, Redwood can route to compatible model variants, but for this POC we will keep routing in-region unless you allow fallback; we can test fallback scenarios separately.

[11:59] Tasha: we'll also review data retention; any logs older than 90 days should be archived.

[12:05] Ethan: noted. we'll include retention config options.

[12:20] Samir: ok thanks everyone.

[12:24] Ethan: thanks all  we'll follow up with the pack and invite for the walkthrough.

[12:30] Meeting end.
